t.7.45.1: Then, when the night had dawned, Lakṣmaṇa, dejected in spirit, spoke these words to Sumantra with a mouth that was drying up.
t.7.45.2: O charioteer, quickly yoke the horses to the finest chariot, and from the royal palace bring Sītā's beautiful seat, well spread with coverings.
t.7.45.3: For Sītā must be taken by me from the royal palace to the hermitage of the great sages of virtuous deeds; let the chariot be brought quickly.
t.7.45.4: Sumantra, saying "So be it," brought a chariot of most splendid appearance, yoked with excellent horses and well spread with a comfortable couch.
t.7.45.5: Having brought it, he said to Saumitri, who increased the joy of his friends: "This chariot has arrived; let whatever must be done be done, O lord."
t.7.45.6: Thus addressed by Sumantra, that Lakṣmaṇa, bull among men, entered the royal palace, approached Sītā, and spoke to her.
t.7.45.7: O queen, by the command of our king, you are to be quickly taken by me to the auspicious hermitage of the sages on the bank of the Gaṅgā.
t.7.45.8: Thus addressed by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, Vaidehī felt incomparable joy and welcomed the journey.
t.7.45.9: Taking those very costly garments and various jewels, Vaidehī set about to depart.
t.7.45.10: "I shall give these ornaments to the wives of the sages." Saumitri said, "So be it," and, seating Maithilī in the chariot, he set out with swift horses, mindful of Rāma's command.
t.7.45.11: Then Sītā said to Lakṣmaṇa, the increaser of good fortune: "O delight of the Raghus, today I see many inauspicious signs."
t.7.45.12: My eye throbs today, and a trembling arises in my limbs; and, O Saumitri, I perceive my heart as if it were unwell.
t.7.45.13: Great is my longing, and great too is my unrest; and I see the earth as though it were empty, O wide-eyed one.
t.7.45.14: May all be well with that brother of yours together with his brothers, and with all my mothers-in-law alike, O hero.
t.7.45.15: "May there be well-being for the living beings in the city and in the countryside as well": thus, with joined palms, Sītā entreated the deities.
t.7.45.16: Having heard that matter, Lakṣmaṇa bowed his head to Maithilī and boldly said, "So be it," though his heart was withering within him.
t.7.45.17: Then, having taken up lodging in a hermitage on the bank of the Gomatī, Saumitri rose again at daybreak and spoke to the charioteer.
t.7.45.18: Yoke the chariot quickly! Today I shall bear the waters of the Bhāgīrathī upon my head, just as Tryambaka did upon the mountain.
t.7.45.19: Having quickly inspected the horses and yoked the mind-swift steeds to the chariot, the charioteer, his palms joined in reverence, said to Vaidehī, "Mount the chariot."
t.7.45.20: At the charioteer's word, Sītā mounted the excellent chariot, together with Saumitri and the wise Sumitra.
t.7.45.21: Then, having journeyed for half a day and beholding the waters of the Bhāgīrathī, the dejected Lakṣmaṇa wept aloud with a great cry.
t.7.45.22: But Sītā, deeply concerned, seeing Lakṣmaṇa in distress, spoke these words: "O knower of dharma, why is it that you are weeping?"
t.7.45.23: Now that we have reached the bank of the Jāhnavī, which I have long desired, why, Lakṣmaṇa, do you make me sad at a time of joy?
t.7.45.24: You are ever devoted at Rāma's feet, O bull among men; have you, separated from him for two nights, been overcome by grief?
t.7.45.25: Rāma is dear to me too, Lakṣmaṇa, as dear as life itself, yet I do not grieve like this; so do not be so childish.
t.7.45.26: Carry me across the Gaṅgā and show me the ascetics; then I shall give you riches, garments and ornaments.
t.7.45.27: Then, having paid due reverence to the great sages and having stayed there for one night, we shall return again to that city.
t.7.45.28: Having heard her words, Lakṣmaṇa wiped his fair eyes and, wishing to cross the Gaṅgā, brought forward a fine boat.
